title: VPC post-deploy: API handshake, concurrency ramp, and incremental model priming suite
creator: Asha Nair
description: Automate a conservative, observable post-deploy validation suite for Private (VPC) deployments that performs: 1) an API handshake and auth/egress verification, 2) a progressive concurrency ramp to detect contention and queueing, and 3) incremental model priming (small-batch warmup across model shards and quant variants). The goal is a deterministic gating signal used by Terraform/CI to mark an upgrade/deploy as healthy or trigger an automated rollback. This suite complements existing smoke checks by focusing on early contention, transient RPC failures, and model cold-start characteristics rather than steady-state throughput.
acceptance_criteria: CI pipeline can execute the suite against a freshly provisioned VPC control-plane and return a single pass/fail result
API handshake phase verifies SSO/KMS access, outbound vendor egress rules, and TLS handshakes within 3s per endpoint
Concurrency ramp identifies >50ms median queueing added per 10 concurrent clients and surfaces on time-series
Incremental priming warms each active model to under 1.2x of baseline inference latency for small inference (<=64 tokens) within the configured warmup budget
Suite emits structured JSON verdict and a metric bundle (latency percentiles, errors, token/sec) that Console ingest can display
When suite fails, Terraform CI marks the deployment Failed and triggers a documented rollback hook
test_plan: Phase 1: API handshake (10 requests) - verify 200/401/403 behaviors, KMS access, identity token validation, and sample metadata headers
Phase 2: Connectivity matrix - exercise control-plane -> worker lanes across AZs, simulate conservative network loss (10% packet loss via proxy) and validate retry behavior
Phase 3: Concurrency ramp - ramp 1 -> 8 -> 32 clients (3-minute windows), run standard text-generation microbenchmarks (64 tokens) and record queuing and tail latency
Phase 4: Incremental model priming - warm models in tiers: tokenizer-only probe, short-prompt warmup, multi-token streaming prime; verify KV/cache warm-hit rates increase over steps
Phase 5: Failure modes - inject a bad model binary on one replica, ensure suite detects elevated error rate and flags partial degradation
Phase 6: Post-run validation - upload JSON verdict to artifacts, annotate CI run, and capture Console dashboard snapshot link
runbook_steps: 1) Kick off pipeline via terraform apply -auto-approve to create private env (test cluster).
2) Wait for infra tags and DNS propagation (use /scripts/wait_for_dns.sh).
4) Monitor console stream for 'handshake:ok' within first 60s. If missing, stream logs from control-plane auth-proxy and worker agent.
5) Observe concurrency ramp graphs. If p95 latency increases by >2x before hitting target concurrency, pause and capture traces.
6) If verdict == FAIL, invoke rollback: terraform apply -var=rollback=true and notify on #private-deploys channel with snapshot and failure artifacts.
7) For partial failures (models degraded), create ENG ticket and tag release owner; add 'hotfix' label if caused by model artifact mismatch.
metrics_thresholds: Model small-inference latency: median < baseline * 1.2, p95 < baseline * 2
Error rate: total request errors < 0.5% during the full run
Queue length: per-worker queue depth increase at ramp <= 20 requests
Priming success: tokenizer and KV hit-rate >= 60% after incremental priming steps
artifacts: GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1327 - postdeploy priming runner + TF hook

2025-02-12 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented handshake phase in postdeploy-runner; pushed prototype PR. Observed TLS timeout flakiness in one lab AZ—added connectivity matrix test.
2025-02-14 - Claire Zhang (Review): Suggest adding explicit KMS key rotation check and S3 egress rule validation. Marked as optional for first pass.
2025-02-16 - Security (Ben Park): Reviewed threat model for running priming runner in customer VPC. No new concerns; advised logging of token IDs and limited retention.
2025-02-18 - Miguel Ortega: Ran suite against staging-private-1. Found slow p95 at concurrency=32 due to worker-side GC pauses; mitigated by tuning JVM flags on agent and re-ran with pass.
